## Project Overview


<center>  
  
![**Image**. Sierra Nevada Lakes and energy channel utilzation in zooplankton using δ^13^C-AA~ESS~.](output/photos/Conness_mid_up.jpg){width=80%}
 
</center>  

  
Compound specific isotope analysis of individual amino acids (CSIA-AA) is a new and exciting tool in the study of trophic ecology and animal nutrition. CSIA-AA are not constrained by the same spatiotemporal variability and fractionation effects observed in stable isotope analyses (SIA) of bulk tissues (carbons + lipids + proteins). Therefore, CSIA-AA represent a sea change in our ability to understand food webs and  trophic interactions.  

Certain amino acids can only be synthesized *de novo* by primary producers (e.g., bacteria, algae, plants, fungi) and must be acquired by animals through feeding/dietary means. Thus, such amino acids are considered 'essential amino acids (AA~ESS~)' for animals. AA~ESS~ are passed from producers to consumers with limited carbon isotope fractionation, making the carbon isotope analysis of individual AA~ESS~ an ideal tool to examine the sources of carbon in consumers. Moreover, the AA~ESS~ carbon isotope values of different groups of primary producers (e.g., microalgae, macroalgae, C~3~/C~4~/CAM plants) vary due to unique biochemical pathways, pools, and fluxes, allowing primary producers AA~ESS~ carbon isotope patterns (i.e., fingerprints) to be separated with high resolution. AA~ESS~ carbon isotope fingerprints can be used to identify the sources of AA~ESS~ supporting consumers and the proportional contributions of different primary producers to consumer diets and/or food chains.

Terrestrial energy channels (known as allochthonous energy channels in aquatic systems) are a resource of energy and nutrients for aquatic consumers and ecosystems, although their significance can vary greatly across space and time. Zooplankton prefer (and require) the high fatty acid content of microalgae, which are a vital nutritional source and considered the base of an important autochthonous energy channel in most aquatic systems.Terrestrial resources entering lakes can lead to browning through the leaching dissolved organic matter and subsequently, a decrease in microalgae productivity as light is attenuated. In such a case, allochthonous energy channels may limit primary production, decreasing the importance of autochthonous energy channels, and provide an important alternative resource for consumers that are able to utilize the abundant (although potentially low quality) terrestrial nutritional sources.

Here, we used CSIA-AA to ask whether zooplankton in high elevation alpine Lakes of the Sierra Nevada Mountains obtain their AA~ESS~ from in-water producers (particulate organic matter dominated by microalgae and benthic algae) or from terrestrial C~3~ plants (sedges, pines, and broadleaf deciduous trees). We sampled 7 Lakes and 1 dystropic pond across an elevation gradient (2500-3200m) and measured environmental conditions (temperature, pH, DOC, TN, TP, chlorophyll-*a*). We analyzed the AA~ESS~ carbon isotope values of three primary producer groups and zooplankton consumers as both a community size-fraction (>350um) and individual taxa.

### Bulk Tissue Carbon and Nitrogen Isotope Values from Symons et al. 2019
Data here is from:  
*Symons, C. C., M. A. Schulhof, H. B. Cavalheri, and J. B. Shurin. 2019. Antagonistic effects of temperature and dissolved organic carbon on fish growth in California mountain Lakes. Oecologia 189: 231–241. doi:10.1007/s00442-018-4298-9*. 

In this study, they sampled fish, grass, pines, zooplankton, and POM for bulk tissue carbon and nitrogen isotope analyses. The figure shows that there is considerable overlap and high variance in the isotopic composition of these groups, making it difficult to determine relative allochthonous and autochthonous contributions to consumers.
```{r Bulk SIA Symons, fig.dim= c(6,4), fig.cap="**Figure S1**. Biplot of bulk tissue stable isotope analysis for carbon (δ^13^C) and nitrogen (δ^15^N) in fish, grasses, pines, POM, and zooplankton from montane Lakes in the Eastern Sierra Nevada Mountains of California (data from Symons et al. 2019)."}

# read in the bulk tissue stable isotope data set from Symons et al. 2019
bulk.iso <- read.csv("data/Symons iso data/Symons_Yos_bulkSIA.csv")

# make a biplot (d13C vs d15N)
d13C.d15N <- ggplot(bulk.iso, aes(x = d13C, y = d15N, fill = Type, shape = Type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "black", alpha=0.8) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(22,25,25,24,21)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orchid", "lightgoldenrod3", "lightsalmon3", "dodgerblue", "gray40")) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(color = Type)) +
  scale_color_manual(values =c ("orchid", "lightgoldenrod3", "lightsalmon3", "dodgerblue", "gray40")) +
  xlab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C, " ("^o,"/"[o][o],", V-PDB)"))) +
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{15}, N, " ("^o,"/"[o][o],", Air)"))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-45, -5), ylim = c(-6, 10)) +
  theme_classic() +
 Fig.formatting

### AA~ESS~ Carbon Isotope Values
Read in the full data set (corrected using the NMX in-house reference material; not to be confused with mean-normalized data) and pull out just the essential amino acid (AA~ESS~) data, then subset by sample **Type**.  
- We will be excluding Lysine due to poor peak size and/or separation.
```{r essAA load}
# read in the essential amino acid carbon isotope data set generated for this study
SNL.d13C.aa <- read.csv("data/Sierra Nevada Lakes AA d13C Data NMX standard_update.csv")

# pull out just the ess AA values (excluding Lys)
SNL.ess <- data.frame(SNL.d13C.aa$SampleID, SNL.d13C.aa$Ile13C, 
                      SNL.d13C.aa$Leu13C, SNL.d13C.aa$Phe13C,
                      SNL.d13C.aa$Thr13C, SNL.d13C.aa$Val13C)

# rename columns
colnames(SNL.ess) <- c("SampleID", "Ile", "Leu", "Phe", "Thr", "Val")
SNL.ess$SampleID <- as.character(SNL.ess$SampleID)

# read in metadata and merge with SNL.ess data frame
meta <- read.csv("data/All_sample_meta.csv") ### SNL-ZOOP-GFF12A is in the metadata but not our actual data set

SNL.ess.meta <- merge.data.frame(meta, SNL.ess, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "SampleID")
SNL.ess.meta <- SNL.ess.meta[!(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "TB-tanks"),]

# make a new level for "Elevation" (in m), "0" for ordering, but actually is "NA"
SNL.ess.meta$elevation..m <- ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "Lukens", "2513",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "MayPond", "2714",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "Sunrise2", "2830",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "Blue", "3054",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "Greenstone", "3091",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "Cascade", "3140",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "EasternBrook", "3155",
                            ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Lake == "Granite2", "3178",
                                    "0"))))))))

# add a "phy.group" column
SNL.ess.meta$phy.group <- ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == "calanoid", "copepoda",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == "calanoid_cyclopoid", "copepoda",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == "Ceriodaphnia", "cladocera",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == "Daphnia", "cladocera",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == "Holopedium", "cladocera",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == "Ceriodaphnia", "cladocera",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Type == ">350um", ">350um",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Group == "Terrestrial Plants", "Plants",
                          ifelse(SNL.ess.meta$Group == "Algae", "Algae", "POM")))))))))


# make an ID column and run the mean normalization procedure
SNL.ess.meta$ID <- 1:nrow(SNL.ess.meta)
for(i in 1:length(SNL.ess.meta$ID)){
  SNL.ess.meta$Ile.n[i] <- (SNL.ess.meta$Ile[i]-mean(as.numeric(SNL.ess.meta[i,6:10])))
  SNL.ess.meta$Leu.n[i] <- (SNL.ess.meta$Leu[i]-mean(as.numeric(SNL.ess.meta[i,6:10])))
  SNL.ess.meta$Phe.n[i] <- (SNL.ess.meta$Phe[i]-mean(as.numeric(SNL.ess.meta[i,6:10])))
  SNL.ess.meta$Thr.n[i] <- (SNL.ess.meta$Thr[i]-mean(as.numeric(SNL.ess.meta[i,6:10])))
  SNL.ess.meta$Val.n[i] <- (SNL.ess.meta$Val[i]-mean(as.numeric(SNL.ess.meta[i,6:10])))
}

# reorder the columns
SNL.ess.meta.ordered<- SNL.ess.meta %>% 
  dplyr::select(SampleID, Lake, elevation..m, Group, Type, orig.class, phy.group, 
                Ile, Leu, Phe, Thr, Val, Ile.n, Leu.n, Phe.n, Thr.n, Val.n)
```


#### Individual AA~ESS~
Arrange and format the data frame for ggplot. We will use this data for linear model tests to determine which (if any)  AA~ESS~ carbon isotope values are different among each **Group**. 
```{r essAA df formatting, collapse=TRUE}

# make new level for "phy.group" based on taxonomy
EAA.df.wide <- SNL.ess.meta.ordered # rename

# subset by Type using the SampleID
plants <- EAA.df.wide[substr(EAA.df.wide$SampleID,1,11) == "SNL-TERPLA-",]
pom <- EAA.df.wide[substr(EAA.df.wide$SampleID,1,8) == "SNL-POM-",]
algae <- EAA.df.wide[substr(EAA.df.wide$SampleID,1,4) == "ALR-",]
zoops <- EAA.df.wide[substr(EAA.df.wide$SampleID,1,9) == "SNL-ZOOP-",]

# subset ess AA data for terrestrial plants
Ile.plants <- as.data.frame(cbind(plants$Group, plants$Lake, "Isoleucine", plants$Ile, plants$Ile.n))
Leu.plants <- as.data.frame(cbind(plants$Group, plants$Lake, "Leucine", plants$Leu, plants$Leu.n))
Phe.plants <- as.data.frame(cbind(plants$Group, plants$Lake, "Phenylalanine", plants$Phe, plants$Phe.n))
Thr.plants <- as.data.frame(cbind(plants$Group, plants$Lake, "Threonine", plants$Thr, plants$Thr.n))
Val.plants <- as.data.frame(cbind(plants$Group, plants$Lake, "Valine", plants$Val, plants$Val.n))

plants.reshape.df <- rbind(Ile.plants, Leu.plants, Phe.plants, Thr.plants, Val.plants)
colnames(plants.reshape.df) <- c("Group", "Lake", "EAA", "d13C", "d13C.n")

# subset ess AA data for POM
Ile.pom <- as.data.frame(cbind(pom$Group, pom$Lake, "Isoleucine", pom$Ile, pom$Ile.n))
Leu.pom <- as.data.frame(cbind(pom$Group, pom$Lake, "Leucine", pom$Leu, pom$Leu.n))
Phe.pom <- as.data.frame(cbind(pom$Group, pom$Lake, "Phenylalanine", pom$Phe, pom$Phe.n))
Thr.pom <- as.data.frame(cbind(pom$Group, pom$Lake, "Threonine", pom$Thr, pom$Thr.n))
Val.pom <- as.data.frame(cbind(pom$Group, pom$Lake, "Valine", pom$Val, pom$Val.n))

pom.reshape.df <- rbind(Ile.pom, Leu.pom, Phe.pom, Thr.pom, Val.pom)
colnames(pom.reshape.df) <- c("Group", "Lake", "EAA", "d13C", "d13C.n")

# subset ess AA data for algae
Ile.algae <- as.data.frame(cbind(algae$Group, algae$Lake, "Isoleucine", algae$Ile, algae$Ile.n))
Leu.algae <- as.data.frame(cbind(algae$Group, algae$Lake, "Leucine", algae$Leu, algae$Leu.n))
Phe.algae <- as.data.frame(cbind(algae$Group, algae$Lake, "Phenylalanine", algae$Phe, algae$Phe.n))
Thr.algae <- as.data.frame(cbind(algae$Group, algae$Lake, "Threonine", algae$Thr, algae$Thr.n))
Val.algae <- as.data.frame(cbind(algae$Group, algae$Lake, "Valine", algae$Val, algae$Val.n))

algae.reshape.df <- rbind(Ile.algae, Leu.algae, Phe.algae, Thr.algae, Val.algae)
colnames(algae.reshape.df) <- c("Group", "Lake", "EAA", "d13C", "d13C.n")

# subset ess AA data for zooplankton
Ile.zoops <- as.data.frame(cbind(zoops$Group, zoops$Lake, "Isoleucine", zoops$Ile, zoops$Ile.n))
Leu.zoops <- as.data.frame(cbind(zoops$Group, zoops$Lake, "Leucine", zoops$Leu, zoops$Leu.n))
Phe.zoops <- as.data.frame(cbind(zoops$Group, zoops$Lake, "Phenylalanine", zoops$Phe, zoops$Phe.n))
Thr.zoops <- as.data.frame(cbind(zoops$Group, zoops$Lake, "Threonine", zoops$Thr, zoops$Thr.n))
Val.zoops <- as.data.frame(cbind(zoops$Group, zoops$Lake, "Valine", zoops$Val, zoops$Val.n))

zoops.reshape.df <- rbind(Ile.zoops, Leu.zoops, Phe.zoops, Thr.zoops, Val.zoops)
colnames(zoops.reshape.df) <- c("Group", "Lake", "EAA", "d13C", "d13C.n")

# create a compiled data frame
EAA.df.long <- rbind(plants.reshape.df, pom.reshape.df, algae.reshape.df, zoops.reshape.df)

EAA.df.long$EAA <- recode_factor(EAA.df.long$EAA,
                                 Isoleucine = "Ile",
                                 Leucine = "Leu",
                                 Phenylalanine = "Phe",
                                 Threonine = "Thr",
                                 Valine = "Val")

EAA.df.long$Lake <- factor(EAA.df.long$Lake,
                           levels=c("Lukens", "MayPond", "Sunrise2", "Blue", "Greenstone",
                                    "Cascade", "EasternBrook", "Granite2"))

# restructure the compiled data frame
EAA.df.long$Group<-as.factor(EAA.df.long$Group)
EAA.df.long$EAA<-as.factor(EAA.df.long$EAA)
EAA.df.long$d13C<-as.numeric(EAA.df.long$d13C)
EAA.df.long$d13C.n<-as.numeric(EAA.df.long$d13C.n)
```


##### Boxplots: raw & mean-normalized essential amino acid carbon isotope values
We see clear effects of sample **Lake** and **Type** that reflect elevation (possibly in interaction with other environmental factors) as well as biology, notably in benthic algae.  *This is Figure S3A-B*.

Mean normalization of essential amino acid carbon isotope values is recommended to handle such variation and allow for group comparisons:  
`Larsen, T., T. Hansen, and J. Dierking. 2020. Characterizing niche differentiation among marine consumers with amino acid δ13C fingerprinting. Ecol. Evol. 10: 7768–7782. doi:10.1002/ece3.6502`. 

```{r EssAA boxplot, fig.dim=c(5,4), results='hide', fig.cap="**Figure S3**. Boxplot of *(A)* measured and *(B)* mean-normalized essential amino acids (AA~EES~) δ^13^C values for benthic algae, terrestrial plants, particulate organic matter (POM), and zooplankton in aquatic habitats in the Eastern Sierras Nevada mountains."}

# now that the data is appropriately structured, make boxplots of AA~ESS~ carbon isotope values as a function of Group (algae, POM, terrestrial plants, zooplankton) 

# color palette for algae, POM, terrestrial plants, and zooplankton, respectively
colors2 <- c("springgreen4", "dodgerblue", "lightsalmon3", "gray50")

# create boxplots of raw essential amino acid carbon isotope values (Fig. S3A)
EAA.box <- ggplot(EAA.df.long, aes(x = EAA, y = d13C, fill = Group))+
  geom_boxplot(color = "black", alpha =0.9)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors2)+ 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C, " ("^o,"/"[o][o],")"),)) +
  xlab(element_blank()) +
  theme_classic() +
  Fig.formatting +
  guides(fill = "none")

# create boxplots of mean-normalized essential amino acid carbon isotope values (Fig. S3B)
# check order if setting label names, levels(EAA.df.long$Group)
EAA.box.nrm <- ggplot(EAA.df.long, aes(x = EAA, y = d13C.n, fill = Group))+
  geom_boxplot(color = "black", alpha=0.9)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors2,
                    labels = c("Benthic Algae", "POM", "Terrestrial Plants", "Zooplankton")) + 
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13}, C[norm]," ("^o,"/"[o][o],")"),)) +
  xlab(element_blank()) +
  theme_classic() +
  Fig.formatting

# combine the raw and mean-normalized essential amino acid carbon isotope value boxplots into one figure and export 
EAA.box.raw.nrm <- plot_grid(EAA.box, EAA.box.nrm, rel_widths = c(1.65, 2.2), labels = c("A", "B"))

### VIEW FIGURE S3 ###
EAA.box.raw.nrm
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/FigS3.SNL.EssAA.Boxplot_rev.pdf", width = 11, height = 5)
dev.off()

##### Facet means: raw & mean-normalized essential amino acid carbon isotope values
Make point-line plots (mean +/-SE) for the individual AA~ESS~ carbon isotope values, both raw and mean-normalized. Do this for each primary producer **Group** (algae, POM, terrestrial plants) and zooplankton. This will allow us to evaluate effects of mean-normalization on different groups. *This is Figure S4A-B*.
```{r ESS zoop by site, results='hide', fig.dim=c(5,4), collapse=TRUE, fig.cap="**Figure S3**. Mean (± standard error) δ^13^C values of individual essential amino acids in producers and plankton. Panel *(A)* is raw, non-normalized data and panel *(B)* is mean-normalized data."}

# group by sample Type, Lake, and EAA, then calculate the mean d13C for EAA for each Group
EAA.long.grouped <- EAA.df.long %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  group_by(Lake, .add = TRUE) %>%
  group_by(EAA, .add = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(Mean.d13C = mean(d13C, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), 
                   SD.d13C = sd(d13C, na.rm = TRUE), 
                   SE.d13C = SD.d13C/sqrt(n),
                   Mean.d13C.n = mean(d13C.n, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), 
                   SD.d13C.n = sd(d13C.n, na.rm = TRUE), 
                   SE.d13C.n = SD.d13C.n/sqrt(n)) 


# set dodge parameters
dodge = position_dodge(width = 0.40)

# plot the raw essential amino acid carbon isotope values (Fig. S4A)
indiv.EAA.plot <- ggplot(EAA.long.grouped, aes(x = EAA, y = Mean.d13C, fill = Lake)) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ Group)+
  theme_bw() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean.d13C-SE.d13C, ymax = Mean.d13C+SE.d13C, color = Lake), 
                position = dodge, width = 0.0, linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_line(data = EAA.long.grouped, 
            aes(x = EAA, y = Mean.d13C, color = Lake, group = Lake), position=dodge, linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 3, shape = 21, color = "black", position = dodge, aes(color = Lake)) +
  ylab(expression(paste(delta^{13},C," ("^o,"/"[o][o],")"),)) +
  xlab(element_blank())+
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +

#### Linear models: AA~ESS-norm~ 
Test for differences in individual EAA carbon isotope values among the four **Groups** (primary producers [algae, POM, terrestrial plants], zooplankton). Which amino acids are different across Groups?
- These models are combined into Table S3 in the supporting information for the manuscript.
- Plots of individual AA~ESS-norm~ carbon isotope values by site are displayed in Figure S4B.

```{r linear models, results='hide', fig.show='hide', collapse=TRUE}

##################### MEAN-NORMALIZED DATA ####################
# testing differences in EAA among Groups using linear models #
###############################################################

# first, set the factor levels and make factors for columns
make.fac <- c("Group", "orig.class", "phy.group", "Lake")
EAA.df.wide[make.fac] <- lapply(EAA.df.wide[make.fac], factor)
str(EAA.df.wide)

# get the raw data frame re-organized for the analyses
ESS.df.raw <- EAA.df.wide %>%
  dplyr::select(SampleID, Lake, elevation..m, Group, Type, orig.class, phy.group,
                Ile, Leu, Phe, Thr, Val)

# get the mean-normalized data frame re-organized for the analyses
ESS.df.norm <- EAA.df.wide %>%
  dplyr::select(SampleID, Lake, elevation..m, Group, Type, orig.class, phy.group,
                Ile.n, Leu.n , Phe.n, Thr.n, Val.n)

#####################
# look at assumptions
for(i in c(8:12)){
  Y <- ESS.df.norm[,i]
  full <- lm(Y ~ Group, data = ESS.df.norm, na.action = na.exclude)
  R <- resid(full) #save glm residuals
  
  op <- par(mfrow = c(2,2), mar = c(5,4,1,2), pty = "sq")
  plot(full, add.smooth = FALSE, which = 1)
  QQ <- qqnorm(R, main = colnames(ESS.df.norm)[i]) 
  QQline <- qqline(R)
  hist(R, xlab = "Residuals", main = colnames(ESS.df.norm)[i])
}

##############################################################
# run the linear models to see which EAA differ among Groups #
##############################################################

### Table S3 ###

# Isoleucine
Ile.n.mod <- lm(Ile.n ~ Group, data = ESS.df.norm)
print(anova(Ile.n.mod), digits = 4) # p=0.027
plot(allEffects(Ile.n.mod), ylab = "Ile.n", par.strip.text = list(cex = 0.7))

posthoc.Ile <- emmeans(Ile.n.mod, ~ Group)
multcomp::cld(posthoc.Ile, Letters = letters) # Plants (A), Algae (A), POM (A), Zoop (A)


# Leucine
Leu.n.mod <- lm(Leu.n ~ Group, data = ESS.df.norm)
print(anova(Leu.n.mod), digits = 4) # p<0.001
plot(allEffects(Leu.n.mod), ylab = "Leu.n", par.strip.text = list(cex = 0.7))

posthoc.Leu.n <- emmeans(Leu.n.mod, ~ Group)
multcomp::cld(posthoc.Leu.n, Letters = letters) # Plants (A), Zoop (B), POM (C), Algae (C)


# Phenylalanine
Phe.n.mod <- lm(Phe.n ~ Group, data = ESS.df.norm)
print(anova(Phe.n.mod), digits = 4) # p<0.001
plot(allEffects(Phe.n.mod), ylab = "Phe.n", par.strip.text = list(cex = 0.7))

posthoc.Phe.n <- emmeans(Phe.n.mod, ~ Group)
multcomp::cld(posthoc.Phe.n, Letters = letters) # Zoop (A), POM (B), Algae (B), Plants (B)


# Threonine
Thr.n.mod <- lm(Thr.n ~ Group, data = ESS.df.norm)
print(anova(Thr.n.mod), digits = 4) # p<0.001
plot(allEffects(Thr.n.mod), ylab = "Thr.n", par.strip.text = list(cex = 0.7))

posthoc.Thr.n <- emmeans(Thr.n.mod, ~ Group)
multcomp::cld(posthoc.Thr.n, Letters = letters) # POM (A), Algae (AB), Zoop (B), Plants (C)


# Valine 
Val.n.mod <- lm(Val.n ~ Group, data = ESS.df.norm)
print(anova(Val.n.mod), digits = 4) # p<0.001
plot(allEffects(Val.n.mod), ylab = "Val.n", par.strip.text = list(cex = 0.7))

posthoc.Val.n <- emmeans(Val.n.mod, ~ Group)
multcomp::cld(posthoc.Val.n, Letters = letters) # Algae (A), Plants (B), Zoop (B), POM (B)

```

### Multivariate analyses
Using the AA~ESS-norm~ δ^13^C data, we will use a PERMANOVA to test whether the four Groups (POM, algae, terrestrial plants, zooplankton) differ in multivariate space. Considering we observed significant site-level differences due to isotopic variation at the base of the food web, we use mean-normalized data.  

#### Permanova: **Group** effects 
Use Permanova to test for differences among sites in normalized δ^13^C values of sources and zooplankton.

*Group effects*  
- Investigate mean-normalized data.
- Test using all four Groups: are there differences among zooplankton, algae, POM and/or terrestrial plants?
- Run PERMANOVA to test for Group effects.
- This is part of Table S4.

This PERMANOVA `EAA.norm.perm.Group` uses *normalized data* to test for differences among algae, POM, terrestrial plants, and zooplankton (pooled).
```{r permanova normalized groups}

# create a new data frame by dropping Lake and phy.group
ESS.norm.perm <- ESS.df.norm %>% dplyr::select(-c(SampleID, elevation..m, orig.class))

# factors: Group (algae, POM, terrestrial plants, zooplankton)
Group.n.fac <- ESS.norm.perm %>% 
  dplyr::select(Group)

# response variables: each EAA
ESS.n.dat <- ESS.norm.perm %>% 
  dplyr::select(Ile.n, Leu.n, Phe.n, Thr.n, Val.n)

################### NORMALIZED DATA ####################
# run a PERMANOVA to test for differences among Groups #
########################################################

# run PERMANOVA
set.seed(51)
EAA.norm.perm.Group <- adonis2(ESS.n.dat ~ Group, data = Group.n.fac, 
                               permutations = 999, method = "euclidian", by = "terms")
EAA.norm.perm.Group # Groups: different at p=0.001, R2=0.54

# run pairwise
set.seed(51)
pairwise.adonis(ESS.n.dat, factors = c(Group.n.fac$Group), sim.method = "euclidian", p.adjust.m = "none")
# all groups differ from each other

###########################################################
# what if just the three sources? (spoiler: same outcome) #
###########################################################

# drop zooplankton
ESS.norm.perm.source <- ESS.norm.perm[!(ESS.norm.perm$Group == "Zooplankton"),]
ESS.norm.dat.source <- ESS.norm.perm.source %>% dplyr::select(Ile.n, Leu.n, Phe.n, Thr.n, Val.n)
Source.n.fac <- ESS.norm.perm.source %>% dplyr::select(Group)

# run PERMANOVA
set.seed(51)
EAA.perm.Source<-adonis2(ESS.norm.dat.source ~ Group, data = Source.n.fac, 
                         permutations = 999, method = "euclidian", by = "terms")
EAA.perm.Source # Groups: different at p=0.001, R2=0.61

# run pairwise
set.seed(51)
pairwise.adonis(ESS.norm.dat.source, factors = c(Source.n.fac$Group), sim.method = "euclidian", p.adjust.m = "none")
# all groups differ from each other

```

```{r permanova raw TO CUT, eval=FALSE}
**** I think we drop this now. Emphasis is on mean-normalized data***
#This PERMANOVA `EAA.raw.perm.Group` uses *measured (non-normalized)* data to test for differences among algae, POM, terrestrial plants, and zooplankton (pooled).

ESS.raw.perm <- ESS.df.raw %>% dplyr::select(-c(SampleID, elevation..m, orig.class))

### LDA 
Use a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to characterize the fingerprints of primary producers (e.g., AA~ESS~ sources) and classify zooplankton with one of these AA~ESS~ sources.  

#### LDA: Train Primary Producers
LDA has an internal normalization procedure (there is no difference in output for data that are mean-normalized versus those that are not). Therefore, we use the measured (NOT mean-normalized) data for all subsequent analyses, including LDA and mixing models. We first train the LDA using the primary producers only, and inspect the error rate/model accuracy using a jackknifed, leave-one-out cross-validation procedure.

Training LDA for three AA~ESS sources (benthic algae, POM, terrestrial plants)
```{r LDA primary producers training, results='hide'}

# full data = 'EAA.df.wide'
prod <- EAA.df.wide[!(EAA.df.wide$Group == "Zooplankton"),]
prod$Group<-droplevels(prod$Group) # drop zooplankton level

#Run an LDA with a jackknifing model fit to look at error rate
#'CV = TRUE' makes the LDA run a jackknifed - leave one out - model fit
All.lda <- lda(Group ~ Ile + Leu + Phe + Thr + Val, data = prod, CV = TRUE)

#Create a table which compares the classification from the LDA model to the actual classification
All.reclass <- table(prod$Group, All.lda$class)

#Total percent of samples correctly classified is the sum of the diagonal of this table: 88.9%
sum(diag(prop.table(All.reclass)))

mean(All.lda$class == prod$Group) # mean accuracy

#Percent of each producer Group correctly reclassified: 77.8% algae, 100% plants, 87.5% POM
diag(prop.table(All.reclass, 1))

#Create a training LDA function from the library data
#Note - you can't use the 'All.lda' object above because the 'CV = TRUE' command was used to create it, and for some reason this won't work with the predict() function
All.train <- lda(Group~ Ile + Leu + Phe + Thr + Val, data = prod)
All.train

# save as txt file
sink("output/LDA_Train_Info.txt")
print(All.train)
sink()

#plot LD1 and LD2 to show the sources
Source.LDA <- ggord(All.train,prod$Group, arrow=0,
      txt = NULL, veclsz = 0, vectyp="blank",# remove vectors and arrows
      cols = c("springgreen4","dodgerblue", "lightsalmon3"), grp_title = "Producers",
      ellipse_pro = 0.95, xlim = c(-6,6), ylim = c(-5,5)) + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = 'top')

#view plot, not used in manuscript
Source.LDA

#Write a csv file for the coefficients of LD1/2
lda.info <- as.data.frame(All.train$scaling)
write.csv(lda.info, "output/SNL_Producers_LDA_loadings_NMX.csv", row.names=FALSE)

#Create a data frame with these LDA coordinates
AllProdPredict <- data.frame(Group = prod$Group, SampleID = prod$SampleID, predict(All.train)$x)

#Write a csv file for the LDA coordinates
write.csv(AllProdPredict, "output/SNL_Producers_LDA_coords_NMX.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


#### LDA: Classify zooplankton
Classify zooplankton within this LDA model. Zooplankton will classify with benthic algae, POM, or terrestrial plants. LDA coordinates (LD1 and LD2) can be used in subsequent mixing models, however, using the actual data (mean-normalized data here) directly in mixing model is advisable, albeit the 2 approaches often yeild similar results.
```{r LDA Zoop1}

# full data for zoops only = 'zoops'

#Classify zooplankton
zoop.predict <- predict(object = All.train, newdata = zoops)
zoop.predict.data <- data.frame(SampleID = zoops$SampleID, Type = zoops$Type, Lake = zoops$Lake,
                                zoop.predict$class, zoop.predict$x)

All.reclass <- table(zoops$Group, zoop.predict$class) # 3 as algae, 25 as POM, 0 as plants

#Write a csv file for the zooplankton LDA info
write.csv(zoop.predict.data, "output/SNL_Zooplankton_LDA_info_NMX.csv", row.names=FALSE)

```

Combine training (AA~ESS~ source/primary producer) LDA data with zooplankton LDA data into one unified data frame that includes measured AA~ESS~ δ^13^C values, sampling information, and LDA classifications, and LDA coordinates.
```{r LDA smithing}

##########################################
# combine the zooplankton and source LDA #
##########################################

### Producers
# AllProdPredict original columns are: "Group", "SampleID", "LD1", "LD2"
# rearrange
AllProdPredict.mod <- AllProdPredict %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "Group", "LD1", "LD2")

# rename columns
colnames(AllProdPredict.mod) <- c("SampleID", "orig.class", "LD1", "LD2")

# make new columns to allow merge
AllProdPredict.mod$LD.class <- "Source"

all(prod$SampleID == AllProdPredict.mod$SampleID) #SampleIDs the same, add in Lake
AllProdPredict.mod$Lake <- prod$Lake

# rearrange
AllProdPredict.mod <- AllProdPredict.mod %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "orig.class", "Lake", "LD.class", "LD1", "LD2")

### Zooplankton
# grab columns we want
zoop.predict.data.NMX<- zoop.predict.data %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "Type", "Lake", "zoop.predict.class", "LD1", "LD2")

# rename factors
zoop.predict.data.NMX <- zoop.predict.data.NMX %>% 
       dplyr::rename("orig.class" = "Type")

zoop.predict.data.NMX <- zoop.predict.data.NMX %>% 
       dplyr::rename("LD.class" = "zoop.predict.class")

####### bind the producer and zooplankton data frames
LDA.df<-rbind(zoop.predict.data.NMX, AllProdPredict.mod)

# make new level for "phy.group" based on taxonomy
LDA.df$phy.group<- ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "calanoid", "copepoda",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "calanoid_cyclopoid", "copepoda",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "Ceriodaphnia", "cladocera",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "Daphnia", "cladocera",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "Holopedium", "cladocera",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "Ceriodaphnia", "cladocera",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == ">350um", ">350um",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "Terrestrial Plants", "Plants",
                             ifelse(LDA.df$orig.class == "Algae", "Algae",
                                    "POM")))))))))
# rearrange
LDA.df.simple<- LDA.df %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "LD.class", "LD1", "LD2")

# combine with raw and mean-normalized data
raw.norm.LD.data <- merge(SNL.ess.meta.ordered, LDA.df.simple, by = "SampleID", all.x = TRUE)
write.csv(raw.norm.LD.data, "output/All.essAA.LDA.data.compiled.csv")

############################## select data and arrange
LDA.df<- raw.norm.LD.data %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "Group", "Lake", "elevation..m", "orig.class", 
                "phy.group", "LD.class", "LD1", "LD2")

LDA.df$elevation..m<-as.numeric(LDA.df$elevation..m)

# reorder Lake by relative elevation
LDA.df$Lake<-reorder(LDA.df$Lake, LDA.df$elevation..m)

# reorder factors 
LDA.df$orig.class<-factor(LDA.df$orig.class, levels=c("Algae", "POM", "Terrestrial Plants",
                                                      ">350um", "calanoid", 
                                                      "calanoid_cyclopoid", "Ceriodaphnia",
                                                      "Daphnia", "Holopedium"))
```

```{r LDA Mixsiar setup}
#Load Packages for MixSIAR Models .... should already load in setup chunk, but just in case
#library(MixSIAR)

############
# MIXTURES #

# ZOOPLANKTON 

# create a new data frame with desired columns for the zooplankton consumers (mixtures)
Mix.df.all <- LDA.df %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "orig.class", "phy.group", "Lake", "elevation..m", "LD1", "LD2")

# remove algae, POM, and plants from the data frame
Mix.df <- Mix.df.all[!(Mix.df.all$orig.class == "Algae" | Mix.df.all$orig.class == "POM" |
                         Mix.df.all$orig.class == "Terrestrial Plants"),]
Mix.df$orig.class <- droplevels(Mix.df$orig.class)

# write and export a csv of the zooplankton data frame
write.csv(Mix.df, "output/Mix.df.csv", row.names = FALSE)

###########
# SOURCES #
###########

# BENTHIC ALGAE, POM, PLANTS 

# create a new data frame with desired columns for the primary producers (sources)
Source.df <-  Mix.df.all[(Mix.df.all$phy.group == "Algae" | Mix.df.all$phy.group == "POM" |
                            Mix.df.all$phy.group == "Plants"),]

# drop levels and subset
Source.df$phy.group <- droplevels(Source.df$phy.group)
Source.df <- Source.df %>%
  dplyr::select("phy.group", "LD1", "LD2")

# calculate mean LD1 values for the sources
mean.ld1.df <- aggregate(LD1 ~ phy.group, data = Source.df, FUN = mean)
colnames(mean.ld1.df) <- c("phy.group", "MeanLD1")

# calculate standard deviations of LD1 values for the sources
sd.ld1.df <- aggregate(LD1 ~ phy.group, data = Source.df, FUN = sd)
colnames(sd.ld1.df) <- c("phy.group", "SDLD1")

# calculate mean LD1 values for the sources
mean.ld2.df <- aggregate(LD2 ~ phy.group, data = Source.df, FUN = mean)
colnames(mean.ld2.df) <- c("phy.group", "MeanLD2")

# calculate standard deviations of LD1 values for the sources
sd.ld2.df <- aggregate(LD2 ~ phy.group, data = Source.df, FUN = sd)
colnames(sd.ld2.df) <- c("phy.group", "SDLD2")

# calculate the number of samples for each of the sources
n.df <- aggregate(LD1 ~ phy.group, data = Source.df, FUN = length)
colnames(n.df) <- c("phy.group", "n")

# bind the values calculated above into one data frame
source.agg.df <- cbind(n.df, mean.ld1.df[2], sd.ld1.df[2], mean.ld2.df[2], sd.ld2.df[2])
colnames(source.agg.df) <- c("", "n", "MeanLD1", "SDLD1", "MeanLD2", "SDLD2")

# write and export a csv of the source data frame
write.csv(source.agg.df, "output/source.agg.df.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

#### run the JAGS model

# a posteriori aggregation of sources

### CLEAN MIXSIAR MODEL BY SAMPLEID RESULTS ###

# *By Sample OUTPUT*: Clean and process summary stats for the "by sample model" and generate an output
# read in the summary stats, parse, and make a dataframe, replacing spaces from .txt

SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output <- read.table(
  "output/MixSIAR_models/LDA_SampleID_model/MixSIAR_SampleID_summary_stats_a_posteriori.txt",
  sep = '\t', header = FALSE, skip = 6)

SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output <- as.data.frame(SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output)
colnames(SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output) <- "full.data"

# remove all extra spaces using "squish", make them 1 space only
library(stringr)
SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output$full.data <- str_squish(SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output$full.data)

# rename columns
library(plyr)
samp.mix.1.out<-separate(SAMP.mixSIAR.1.output, full.data,  
                         into = c("factor", "Mean", "SD", "2.5.perc", "5.perc", "25.perc", "50.perc",
                                  "75.perc", "95.perc", "97.5.perc"), sep=" ")

# parse the factors here into 3 columns
new.cols <- stringr::str_split_fixed(samp.mix.1.out$factor, "\\.", 3) %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
       setNames(c("proportion", "Source", "SampleID"))

new.cols <- new.cols %>%
  dplyr::select("SampleID", "Source")

# combine the new, separated columns with the data, verify the levels match, then remove "factor"
Samp.out.cleaned <- cbind(new.cols, samp.mix.1.out[1:10])
Samp.out.cleaned <- Samp.out.cleaned %>%
  dplyr::select(-factor)

Samp.out.cleaned<-na.omit(Samp.out.cleaned)
                          
write.csv(Samp.out.cleaned, "output/MixSIAR_models/LDA_SampleID_model/MixSIAR_SampleID_a_posteriori.df.csv", row.names = FALSE)

colnames(sd.Ile.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "SD.Ile.n")

### Leu mean and SD

colnames(mean.Leu.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "Mean.Leu.n")

# calculate standard deviations of LD1 values for the sources

colnames(sd.Leu.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "SD.Leu.n")

### Phe mean and SD

mean.Phe.n.df <- aggregate(Phe.n ~ phy.group, data = Source.df.n, FUN = mean)
colnames(mean.Phe.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "Mean.Phe.n")

# calculate standard deviations of LD1 values for the sources
sd.Phe.n.df <- aggregate(Phe.n ~ phy.group, data = Source.df.n, FUN = sd)
colnames(sd.Phe.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "SD.Phe.n")

### Thr mean and SD
# calculate mean Leu.n values for the sources
mean.Thr.n.df <- aggregate(Thr.n ~ phy.group, data = Source.df.n, FUN = mean)
colnames(mean.Thr.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "Mean.Thr.n")

# calculate standard deviations of LD1 values for the sources

colnames(sd.Thr.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "SD.Thr.n")

### Val mean and SD
# calculate mean Leu.n values for the sources

colnames(mean.Val.n.df) <- c("phy.group", "Mean.Val.n")

# calculate standard deviations of LD1 values for the sources

#### sample size

# bind the values calculated above into one data frame
source.agg.df.n <- cbind(n.df.size, 
                         mean.Ile.n.df[2], sd.Ile.n.df[2], mean.Leu.n.df[2], sd.Leu.n.df[2],

                               "MeanPhe.n", "SDPhe.n", "MeanThr.n", "SDThr.n", "MeanVal.n", "SDVal.n")

# write and export a csv of the source data frame
write.csv(source.agg.df.n, "output/source.agg.df.norm.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")

Mix.samp.n$Lake<-as.factor(reorder(Mix.samp.n$Lake, Mix.samp.n$elevation..m))
Mix.samp.n$phy.group<-droplevels(Mix.samp.n$phy.group)

Mix.samp.plot.n <- ggplot(data = Mix.samp.n, aes(x = phy.group, y = Mean, fill = Source)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.8)+
  geom_point(aes(color=Source), alpha=0.4, position=position_dodge(0.7))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("dodgerblue", "springgreen4")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray30", "gray30")) +
  ylab("Proportional Contribution") +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylim(0,1)+
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title = expression(paste(AA[ESS], " ", Source)))) +
  theme_classic() + Fig.formatting + guides(color = "none")

#print and save
Mix.samp.plot.n
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/Figxx.mixsiar.nEAA.pdf", width=6, height=7)
dev.off()


#### plot by lake
Mix.lake.plot.n <- ggplot(data = Mix.samp.n, aes(x = Lake, y = Mean, fill = Source)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.8)+
  geom_point(aes(color=Source), alpha=0.4, position=position_dodge(0.7))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("dodgerblue", "springgreen4")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray30", "gray30")) +
  ylab("Proportional Contribution") +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylim(0,1)+

Mix.lake.plot.n
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/Figxx.mixsiar.lake.nEAA.pdf", width=10, height=7)

############### plot as mean-SE
alloch.mean<-aggregate(Mean~Source+ phy.group, data=Mix.samp.n, FUN=mean)

alloch.n<-aggregate(Mean~Source+ phy.group, data=Mix.samp.n, FUN=length)
colnames(alloch.n)<-c("Source", "phy.group", "n")

alloch.SD<-aggregate(Mean~Source+ phy.group, data=Mix.samp.n, FUN=sd)
colnames(alloch.SD)<-c("Source", "phy.group", "SD")

alloch.df<-cbind(alloch.mean, (alloch.SD$SD/sqrt(alloch.n$n)))
colnames(alloch.df)<-c("Source", "phy.group", "mean", "SE")

# plot it
pd <- position_dodge(0.71) #offset for error bars and columns

alloch.mean.plot<-ggplot(alloch.df, aes(x=phy.group, y=mean, color=Source)) +
  geom_point(position = pd, size=3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("dodgerblue", "springgreen4")) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-SE, ymax=mean+SE),size=.5, width=0, position=pd) +
  ylab("Proportional Contribution") +
  ylim(0,1)+
  xlab("")+ theme_bw()

alloch.mean.plot
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/Figxx.mixsiar.mean.pdf", width=5, height=7)
dev.off()

*Combine all data*   
Now that we have more data, combine it with the previous data so that we have a unified dataframe with the sampling information, measured AA~ESS~ data, LD-classification, LD1 coordinate, and mixing model output usin *norm-EAA values*.
```{r generate full data, results='hide'}
#### by sample
#check.names=FALSE prevents an "X" being added to the columns that start with a number
samp.mix.df<-read.csv("output/MixSIAR_models/nEAA_SampleID_model/MixSIAR_SampleID_a_posteriori.df.nEAA.csv",
                      check.names=FALSE) 

samp.mix.reduced<- samp.mix.df %>% 
  dplyr::select(SampleID, Source, Mean, SD)

# extract out the df for the two sources
Auto.mix<-samp.mix.reduced[(samp.mix.reduced$Source=="Autochthonous"),]
colnames(Auto.mix)<-c("SampleID", "Source", "Auto.mean", "Auto.SD")
Auto.mix<- Auto.mix %>% dplyr::select(-Source) # remove this column for merge below

Alloch.mix<-samp.mix.reduced[(samp.mix.reduced$Source=="Allochthonous"),]
colnames(Alloch.mix)<-c("SampleID", "Source", "Alloch.mean", "Alloch.SD")
Alloch.mix<- Alloch.mix %>% dplyr::select(-Source) # remove this column for merge below

# combine
Mixes <- merge.data.frame(Auto.mix, Alloch.mix, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "SampleID", all=TRUE)

# combine zoops and producers, called in from 'EAA.df.wide'
head(EAA.df.wide)

# reduce LDA df for merge
LDA.df.reduced<- LDA.df %>% 
  dplyr::select(SampleID, LD.class, LD1, LD2)

# merge LDA and Mixsiar
MSiar.LD.meta <- merge.data.frame(LDA.df.reduced, Mixes, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "SampleID", all=TRUE)

# merge with all raw and normalized data
MSiar.LD.meta.EAA <- merge.data.frame(EAA.df.wide, MSiar.LD.meta,
                                      by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "SampleID", all=TRUE)

MSiar.LD.meta.EAA <- MSiar.LD.meta.EAA %>% dplyr::select(-elevation..m) # duplicate in merge below

# read in environmental data (loaded above, <-read.csv("data/SNL.envdata.csv"), "SNL.env"
SNL.CSIA.fulldata<-merge.data.frame(SNL.env, MSiar.LD.meta.EAA, by.x = "Lake", by.y = "Lake", all=TRUE)

#### export full data for project
write.csv(SNL.CSIA.fulldata, "output/SNL.CSIA.fulldata.csv")
```
  

### Multiple linear regressions 
Use the proportion of AA~ESS~ from terrestrial plants from the mixing model with a multiple linear regressions analysis to find the environmental conditions that correlate with each other and exhibit a relationship with changes in allochthony for each zooplanton category. 

- First generate the correlation matrix for environmental conditions
- This will determine the model predictors
```{r correlation matrix, results='hide', fig.cap="**Figure** Correlation matrix displaying Pearson’s coefficient (r) between environmental and biogeochemical metrics at eight aquatic habitats in the Eastern Sierras Nevada Mountains. Positive and negative coefficients indicate positive and negative correlations between metrics, respectively."}
# use 'ESS.mods' to run models

# look at % plant contributions by environmental data
mod.data<- SNL.CSIA.fulldata %>%
  dplyr::select(SampleID, Lake, Group, elevation..m, depth..m, temp..C, DO..perc, pH, DOC..mg.L,
                TDN..ug.L, TDP..ug.L, chla..ug.L, phy.group, Ile, Leu, Phe, Thr, Val, LD.class, 
                LD1, LD2, Alloch.mean, Alloch.SD)

# remove Sources
Plant.nut.env<-mod.data[!(mod.data$LD.class=="Source"),] 
Plant.nut.env$Group<- droplevels(Plant.nut.env$Group) # droplevels
Plant.nut.env$phy.group<- droplevels(Plant.nut.env$phy.group) # droplevels
Plant.nut.env$LD.class<- droplevels(Plant.nut.env$LD.class) # droplevels

Plant.nut.env$Alloch.mean<-as.numeric(Plant.nut.env$Alloch.mean)
############# ############# ############# ############# 
############# look at correlation matrix, what variables strongly correlate?

# Install and load the ggcorrplot package

# Keep predictors for the model
reduced_data <- Plant.nut.env %>%
  dplyr::select(elevation..m, temp..C, pH,
                TDN..ug.L, TDP..ug.L, chla..ug.L, DOC..mg.L)

# Compute correlation at 2 decimal places
corr_matrix = round(cor(reduced_data), 2)

# Compute and show the  result
ggcorrplot(corr_matrix, hc.order = TRUE, type = "lower",
          lab = TRUE)

### export it
dev.copy(pdf, "figures/FigS2.correl.matrix.pdf", height=6, width=8)
dev.off()

# from here, TDN, TDP, DOC all correlate with >0.77 (TN and DOC at 0.94!) So only need 1 of these in a multiple linear regression
```

```{r spatial effects}
# any effect of depth or elevation?
mod.mult.spat<-lm(Alloch.mean~elevation..m+ depth..m,
             data=Plant.nut.env)
Anova(mod.mult.spat, Type=2) # significant elevation effect, corresponds with temp effects

# differences among groups?
mod.mult.phy<-lm(Alloch.mean~phy.group+LD.class,
             data=Plant.nut.env)
Anova(mod.mult.phy, Type=2) # differs by phy.group, 
posthoc.phy <- emmeans(mod.mult.phy, ~ phy.group)
multcomp::cld(posthoc.phy, Letters = letters) # >350 (A), Copepod (B), Cladoceran (B)

```

**Multiple regressions for ALL zooplankton** = >350 um, cladocerans, copepods
```{r all zoop multR2, results='hide', fig.keep='none'}
# library(MASS)

# run a full model
mod.mult<-lm(Alloch.mean~temp..C+ pH+TDN..ug.L+chla..ug.L,
             data=Plant.nut.env)

# model fit
summary(mod.mult)

# check distribution and residuals
hist(mod.mult$residuals)
qqnorm(mod.mult$residuals)
qqline(mod.mult$residuals)

sigma(mod.mult)/mean(Plant.nut.env$Alloch.mean) #48% error rate, not awesome. 

# run model selection
all.zoop.mods<-stepAIC(mod.mult, trace=TRUE)

# best model is with temp (p=0.049), TDN (p=0.146). R2-adjust = 0.084, RSE= 0.137
mod.mult.all<-lm(Alloch.mean~temp..C + TDN..ug.L,
             data=Plant.nut.env)
summary(mod.mult.all)
Anova(mod.mult.all, Type=2) # sinificant temp effect

## temp alone
mod.mult.all.reduc<-lm(Alloch.mean~temp..C,data=Plant.nut.env)
summary(mod.mult.all.reduc)
Anova(mod.mult.all.reduc, Type=2) # sinificant temp effect

# temp, all Groups
temp.prop.plant<-ggplot(Plant.nut.env, aes(x=temp..C, y=Alloch.mean)) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, color="purple", alpha=0.2, fill="purple")+
  geom_point(color="violet", size=2.5)+
  ylab("Proportion Plant-EAA")+
  xlab("Temperature (C)")+
  ggtitle("All Zooplankton")+
  annotate("text", x = 15, y = 0.75, label = "R2=0.068, p=0.003", size = 3) +
  ylim(0,0.8)+
  theme_classic()

# N, all Groups
N.prop.plant<-ggplot(Plant.nut.env, aes(x=TDN..ug.L, y=Alloch.mean)) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, color="purple", alpha=0.2, fill="purple")+
  geom_point(color="violet", size=2.5, aes(shape=phy.group))+
  ylab("Proportion Plant-EAA")+
  xlab("TDN (umol/L)")+
  ylim(0,0.8)+
  theme_classic()

```
